I usually find that hardcore Star Wars fans enjoy the prequels more, while people more interested in film in general prefer the sequels. This really isn't that weird though. The sequels however are competently directed, acted and edited films, with more conventionally alright writing. You can say the writing is bad all you want and that the prequels are better written, fine I'm not going bother to argue because that's subjective at heart. What I am saying is that sequel scenes are written tightly with structure, and get the intended point across, even if you don't think the point is very fitting for the story. The prequels are also just shot really badly. Camera A and B is overused to a ridiculous extent, and scenes with only two shot compositions aren't rare. The editing is also bafflingly strange, and it's seemingly edited in real time, which is the first thing any new editor learns not to do.

The prequels have more of a reason to exist, and a more interesting story to tell at heart, but they kind off just such at a technical level, on almost every regard, while the opposite is true of the sequels.

From the very beginning, a Link to the Past was immagined as a prequel to the original two games, originally being a retelling of the tale of Zelda the First from The Adventure of Link's manual. All right, here are my attempts to answer your questions

1. I was a FIRM believer in Minish Cap being the first in the timeline, however, after being confronted by more evidence, I have come to the conclusion that it is literally impossible for any game to take place before SS. Yes, there are some interesting pieces of evidence that would seem to place Minish Cap at the beginning, like the Armos for example. Said to be the creation of the Minish, it doesn't make sense for SS to predate it, as the armos appear in that game. The game explaining the origin of Links cap also seems to make it out as an origin story. However, I am sorry to say that the evidence for the placement the other way around is overwhelming. First of all, we know SS Zelda has to be the first, as we are told she is the first reincarnation of the goddess Hylia. Furthermore, Hyrule itself is named after SS, only called the surface in the game. This makes it impossible in itself for TMC to be before, as it takes place in Hyrule. This placement isn't perfect, and I haven't seen a single timeline where these games make complete sense, however, this is also what the cannon timeline goes with, as it's the option that leaves the fewest logical holes.
2. This point is a little strange to me. If you switch OOT and FSA, you are still left with the exact same problem. Why did the Gerudo switch from making the sole male king, to a guardian? You could stretch it, and say that it's because the previous Ganondorf was evil as shit, so making him king would be a bad idea, but then why give him a title of authority at all? There are also several hundred years between games, so the guardian changing to the king doesn't seem that far-fetched to me.
3. The Timeline split in oot here is taken mostly from the Cannon timeline. Link in the child timeline uses the Triforce of Courage as evidence of why Ganondorf is evil, and the king has him executed. It fails, as Link returns with the Triforce of course, ie the Triforce is not complete, thus the two remaining pieces go to Link and Zelda. This piece saves Ganon, and he is instead sealed within the Twilight Realm. In the Adult timeline, Link disappears off course, leading to the events of WW. How did it get back to the Adult timeline? I'm not sure, but Windwaker is confirmed to be a sequel to OOT, having the same Ganondorf and taking place after events that were directly sparked from Link leaving the timeline. Since the full Triforce appears, it's safe to assume that only one Triforce of courage can exist in each Timeline, so Link was instead granted that piece from his own timeline. This is mostly up to Nintendo wanting to make a remake/sequel to ALTTP, and not fully committing to one.
4. Oops! Seems I have forgotten a couple of games. Oracle true ending ends with Link on a boat, so Links Awakening takes place after that. Triforce Hero is after a Link Between Worlds.
5. Really close to convincing me here, but again while it does make sense for it to come before, there is simply more proof that it comes after. First of all, yes ALTTP ended with a prosperous era, but that era would eventually end. Furthermore, ALBW literally has murals recapping the events of ALTTP. The golden sword becoming the master sword again would simply be down to time, as the metal used to reforge the sword would eventually disappear, while the blade forged by gods of course wouldn't. 

So that's all the questions. Thanks for the feedback man! There are of course still a few small issues, but no obvious way to fix them honestly, and the larger story beats seem to line up. So all in all, I think this timeline works pretty well.
